A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

input.reflection: Tables: traces (abnormal/normal), metrics, metrics_sum, histogram, logs. Traces have service_name, span_name, duration, status code, http method/status. Plan: compare per-service/per-endpoint error rate and latency abnormal vs normal; then check the call chain and resource metrics.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' AS src, service_name, span_name, count(*) n, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=500 OR attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'nor', service_name, span_name, count(*), avg(duration)/1e6, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6, sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=500 OR attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3,2,1

## Investigation summary

The degradation is latency, not errors. I found one root cause, in **ts-order-other-service**, specifically in its database access path. I could not confirm the exact DB-side mechanism because the telemetry has no database metrics.

### Affected endpoints and services

| Service / endpoint | Normal (avg / p95) | Abnormal (avg / p95) | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| ts-order-other-service, `POST /orderOtherService/orderOther/refresh` | ~2.8 ms | ~128 ms avg, max 3.1 s | Origin |
| ts-order-other-service, `GET /orderOtherService/orderOther` | ~3.6 ms | ~676 ms avg, max 3.4 s | Origin |
| ts-admin-order-service, `GET /adminorderservice/adminorder` | ~7.7 ms / ~15 ms | ~399 ms / ~1487 ms | Victim (calls order-other) |
| ts-admin-order-service, POST/PUT/DELETE adminorder | low ms | ~290–770 ms | Victim (calls order-other) |
| ts-ui-dashboard (user-facing) | ~22 ms / ~76 ms | ~35 ms / ~77 ms | Victim, via the refresh and admin paths |

Everything else matches normal within noise. This includes the sibling ts-order-service (~1.7 ms), travel, travel2, route, train, station, user, auth, and verification-code. There are no 5xx codes and no error status codes in any service. Users see slowness, not failures.

### Propagation path

- **Origin:** ts-order-other-service. Its own DB spans are slow: `SELECT ts.orders_other` (p50 0.3 ms, max 3.1 s), `SELECT other.entity.Order`, and `Transaction.commit` (p50 0.2 ms → 205 ms, max 1.9 s). The handler's own work is negligible, so the time is spent inside its DB layer.
- **Callers that inherit the latency:**
  - ts-ui-dashboard calls order-other directly on refresh (~116 ms vs ~1 ms).
  - ts-admin-order-service calls order-other on `GET orderOther` (~704 ms). Its `addOrder`, `updateOrder`, and `deleteOrder` paths also call order-other and are slow.
  - ts-admin-order-service's call to ts-order-service stays fast (~4 ms), which isolates the fault to order-other.

### Timeline

- The fault window is 2026-05-01, roughly 18:44:30 to 18:49:30 UTC.
- During that window, about 20–40% of `SELECT ts.orders_other` calls exceed 100 ms in every 30-second bin.
- Before and after the window, the same spans run at normal latency.

### Why this points to contention or a stall, not CPU

- Pod CPU time moved only from about 48 to 54 units. Memory and GC metrics are flat.
- Only one order-other pod appears in the traces, so the slowness is not isolated to one replica.
- The pattern is an intermittent tail of multi-second stalls inside DB calls and commits. That fits lock waits or a DB-side stall on the orders_other data, not pod saturation.

### Caveats

- The order-other logs show only INFO query-progress messages in the window, with no errors or warnings. Normal logs have 164 WARN entries, which are benign "No content" seat messages.
- I cannot tell from this telemetry whether the blocking is a row or table lock, a long-running transaction, or a database server issue. The on-call team should check order-other's DB connection pool and lock metrics, and the database's active-query and lock-wait views, for 2026-05-01 18:44–18:50 UTC.
